title: Summit Club Membership Holder Requirements Chart
content:
Every membership in the Crestline Summit Club Lounge Memberships range sets the same two personal requirements for its holder — an open Summit membership and a minimum age — and differs in who pays for it, whether it is bought once, and whether it may be granted as a Summit choice benefit.

| Membership | Open Summit membership required to hold and use it | Youngest age of a holder | Paid by | One-time purchase | May be granted as a Summit choice benefit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Summit Club Essential | Yes | 21 years | The member | No | No |
| Summit Club Individual | Yes | 21 years | The member | No | Yes |
| Summit Club Individual Plus | Yes | 21 years | The member | No | No |
| Summit Club Executive | Yes | 21 years | The member | No | No |
| Summit Club Corporate | Yes | 21 years | A corporate travel agreement | No | No |
| Summit Club Lifetime | Yes | 21 years | The member | Yes | No |

## Notes on the chart

- **Summit membership.** For every membership in the range, an open Summit membership is required both to hold the lounge membership and to use it.
- **Age.** The youngest age at which a person may hold any of these memberships is 21 years. A person aged 20 does not meet it; a person who has reached 21 does.
- **Payer.** Summit Club Corporate is paid for by a corporate travel agreement. The other five memberships are paid by the member.
- **One-time purchase.** Summit Club Lifetime is bought with a single one-time purchase; the other five memberships are not one-time purchases.
- **Choice benefit.** Summit Club Individual is the only membership in the range that may be granted as a Summit choice benefit.
